parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Assess data in the intended workflow
parts.body:
Data is ready for a use only when it is fit for that use. A policy archive may be accurate enough for staff to browse but unsafe for an assistant that returns one confident answer: old versions, regional exceptions, or unclear permissions may be hidden in the search results. Begin with the decision or task the system supports. Name the source owner, lawful or authorized use, population, quality requirements, update frequency, lineage, and the person who can correct an error. A generic 'data quality' score cannot settle all of these questions.

Sample actual records across time, teams, and regions. Check completeness, duplicates, conflicting definitions, missing effective dates, and whether the system can distinguish superseded content. For structured data, compare fields with source systems and measure missingness by subgroup. For documents, inspect whether a retrieved passage carries its source version and jurisdiction. Record what proportion fails the intended task and whether the failure can cause inconvenience, financial loss, or an unfair decision.

NIST's AI RMF asks teams to map data and context, measure risks in the intended use, and document ongoing monitoring. The data owner should be able to approve cleanup and explain lineage; the business owner decides whether the resulting limitations are acceptable for the workflow. A pilot that lacks this chain of responsibility will struggle to correct bad answers after launch.

example.title: One archive, different readiness
example.body: An HR policy collection can support a staff search tool after deduplication, but a benefits eligibility assistant needs current regional rules, effective dates, and a reliable way to detect an exception. The same files are not equally ready for both tasks.

exercise.title: Audit a sample
exercise.body: Inspect 20 records or documents for one intended use. Mark owner, region, effective date, version, access class, missing fields, and conflicts. Estimate the failure rate for that use and assign each cleanup action to an owner.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Map data and context

parts.label: Practice
parts.title: Carry permissions through retrieval
parts.body:
A retrieval system can expose restricted information even when its model never memorizes it. The index may contain documents for multiple departments, and a broad search can return a relevant but unauthorized passage. Apply the requester's identity and authorization at retrieval time, test inherited document permissions, and prevent a cached answer or citation from crossing a user's boundary. The source system remains the authority for access; an index needs a reliable way to receive permission changes and removals.

Design the answer so a reviewer can inspect the cited source, version, and effective date. If access is revoked or a document is corrected, define how quickly the index and caches change and how to identify answers that used the old material. Log enough to investigate failures while limiting personal data in logs and setting retention deliberately. Test adversarial queries that ask the assistant to reveal another employee's record or ignore the user's role. The answer should fail safely when the needed source cannot be accessed.

The EU GDPR requires purpose limitation and data minimisation for personal data, with data protection by design and default. In Canada, PIPEDA accountability and safeguards apply where that law governs; provincial and sector rules may add requirements. Neither regime can be reduced to a universal 'keep data in region' rule. Privacy and legal owners should determine transfer, retention, and access obligations for the actual data and service.

example.title: A stale permission
example.body: An employee transfers from payroll to sales. A search index still carries yesterday's payroll access. The assistant must use current authorization before retrieval and test revocation lag, rather than trusting a one-time index build.

exercise.title: Trace a restricted query
exercise.body: Draw the path from sign-in through authorization, retrieval, reranking, model input, answer, citation, cache, and log. At each step, mark who may read personal data and how a revoked permission reaches that component.

sources: European Commission: data protection by design and default
Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada: PIPEDA accountability

parts.label: Operate
parts.title: Fund the cleanup that changes the outcome
parts.body:
Data work should be sequenced by the decisions it unlocks. For an HR assistant, identifying current policies and access classes may matter more than converting every old PDF. Make a readiness backlog with source, defect, affected use cases, error consequence, correction owner, cost, and date. Prefer a small authoritative set for a pilot when the wider archive cannot be reconciled. Exclude a region or topic explicitly rather than returning an uncertain answer that looks final.

Set measurable acceptance criteria for the use. For instance, all sampled answers about leave policy should cite a current, authorized document for the employee's jurisdiction, with a defined error and abstention threshold. The actual threshold depends on stakes and baseline. Test conflicting versions, missing sources, ambiguous questions, and permission changes. Do not count an abstention as a correct answer without examining whether it leaves the worker able to finish the task.

Keep the quality loop after launch. A source owner approves changes, the index update is verified, a regression suite checks affected questions, and a named operator reviews error trends. When a source is retired, record how the system removes it and whether prior outputs require investigation. The CAIO should fund this ongoing stewardship in the business case; the one-time ingestion cost understates the operating commitment.

example.title: A selective cleanup
example.body: The team excludes archived benefit guides and publishes only approved current policies for Ontario and France. It tests both regions and records abstentions for unsupported locations. Wider coverage becomes a separate funded decision.

exercise.title: Prioritize five defects
exercise.body: From your sample audit, rank five cleanup items by expected reduction in decision error per unit of effort. Define an acceptance test, owner, and ongoing update method for the top two.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: Measure and Manage
NIST AI RMF Playbook: Measure performance in context

parts.label: Apply
parts.title: Make a go or no-go recommendation
parts.body:
An executive data-readiness decision needs more than a traffic-light score. Report the intended use, sample method, source coverage, defects by severity, permission controls, regional scope, cleanup cost, and residual risk. Separate a defect the team can repair before pilot from one that changes the project's economics or makes the proposed use inappropriate. Include the fallback when the system lacks an authorized, current source.

Consider three options: pilot with a narrower approved corpus, pay to remediate the wider data estate, or defer the use. The first may create evidence quickly, but it must be clear to users where it does not apply. The second needs a business sponsor because data cleanup can benefit several uses. The third can be right when no owner can maintain the source. Ask who is responsible for incorrect information reaching a customer or worker, and whether that person has a practical way to detect and correct it.

Keep jurisdictional claims precise. A company operating in the EU and Canada may have different lawful bases, notice, retention, and transfer arrangements by data type and entity. The privacy officer and counsel decide those requirements. The CAIO's recommendation should state the design assumptions and the decision that remains with those specialists.

example.title: A conditional go
example.body: Approve a six-week internal HR search pilot limited to current Ontario policies after access testing and source-owner signoff. Do not include employee case files. Expansion to EU staff waits for policy reconciliation and privacy review. This is a hypothetical decision.

exercise.title: Write the gate memo
exercise.body: Make a one-page recommendation for the audited dataset. Choose narrow pilot, remediation, or defer; give the evidence, cost, owner, region, excluded data, acceptance threshold, and next review date.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: documented risk decisions
Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada: PIPEDA principles
